editorial:
You are dropped into a cramped prison cell where four men have spent months planning a daring escape. When Claude Gaspard is moved in, they must decide whether to trust him with their secret. The movie turns that simple choice into a tense, close-up story about friendship, risk, and survival. Every knock on the wall and scrape of metal feels important, and the cell becomes its own small world. You feel every minute of their plan.

The black-and-white photography and long, quiet scenes make the hard work feel real without rushing. The acting is natural, and the digging scenes are surprisingly gripping. It can feel slow if you want nonstop action, and the old-school style may not suit everyone. Still, it is a smart pick for fans of crime dramas and prison stories.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the men finally break through to the sewer and start crawling toward freedom, but their plan has already been betrayed. Claude Gaspard, the newcomer they trusted with every secret, has tipped off the guards. The escape is stopped before anyone gets out, the four original inmates are caught, and Gaspard is left alone with the broken trust.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic prison escape stories and patient crime dramas.
